newsitem.title: JAPAN: New rules for Japan banks cover narrow range - paper.
newsitem.headline: New rules for Japan banks cover narrow range - paper.

text.p: Japan's Finance Ministry (MOF) will not apply mark-to-market accounting standards for banks' stock-related transactions when the new rules are introduced on March 31, 1998, a newspaper reported on Thursday.

The Nikkei Financial Daily reported a ministry draft said that stock-related transactions, including money in trusts (tokkin) and fund trusts which invest in stocks, will not be covered by the new standards.
A MOF official would not confirm the report, saying the ministry was still working out the types of financial instruments to be covered by the new accounting methods.
The new rules will also not cover stocks and bonds for long-term holdings, but will cover commercial paper and overseas certificates of deposit (CDs), the paper said.
Analysts said the draft shows that MOF wants to limit the use of the new accounting rules because of worries about drastic changes in the banking industry.
Japan's parliament passed a special act in June allowing banks and brokers to use mark-to-market accounting methods for derivatives and short-term securities trading.

Currently in Japan, financial products are basically appraised according to the cost at purchase, and realised gains or losses are posted in current income statements only when the positions are closed.
In mark-to-market accounting, unrealised gains or losses in trading accounts must be included in current profit/loss statements.
Banks must get permission from the ministry to use mark-to-market accounting methods.
